name: Brij Mohan Labroo
current_role: Deceased (was Chairman and founder-promoter, Asahi India Glass)
profile: Founder-promoter of Asahi India Glass (AIS), on its board since 1985 and Chairman until his death on 7 November 2022 at age 92. His son Sanjay Labroo now leads AIS as Chairman & MD.
notes: Died 7 Nov 2022 per AIS stock-exchange announcement: https://marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ASAHI-INDIA-GLASS-LIMITED-6494392/news/Asahi-India-Glass-Limited-Announces-Demise-of-Brij-Mohan-Labroo-as-Chairman-42291238 ; https://www.glassworldwide.co.uk/industry-announcements/remembering-mr-brij-mohan-labroo

name: James Charles Hays
current_role: Director (retiring in 2026), Skyward Specialty Insurance Group (NASDAQ: SKWD); founder of Hays Companies
profile: Jim Hays left Aon in Chicago to found Minneapolis-based Hays Companies in 1994, building it into the Upper Midwest's largest independent commercial insurance and benefits broker before selling its insurance operations to Brown & Brown in 2018 for about $705M. He has been a long-time backer and director of Skyward Group, which announced in April 2026 he would retire from its board.
interesting_fact: The 2018 Hays deal (about $705M) was the largest acquisition in Brown & Brown's 75-year history; Hays then had 700+ professionals in 32 offices across 21 states.
deep_cut_fact: Hays started Hays Companies in 1994 with five partners, each of whom put in $300,000 of their own money.

public_contacts.value: Skyward Specialty investor relations site (IR contacts listed there)

notes: Skyward said Peter Hearn would join the board Aug 1, 2026, succeeding Hays, who retires 'later this year' after nearly two decades with Skyward Group (https://investors.skywardinsurance.com/news-releases/news-release-details/industry-leader-peter-hearn-join-board-directors-jim-hays-retire). Low public profile; no personal channels found.

name: Matthew H. Peltz
current_role: Partner and Co-Head of Research, Trian Fund Management; Wendy's director (non-exec Vice Chairman since Nov 2021; verify current board status)
profile: Son of activist investor Nelson Peltz, Matt Peltz joined Trian's investment team in 2008 after two years as a Goldman Sachs investment-banking analyst, and is now a partner and co-head of research. He has sat on Wendy's board since December 2015 and served as non-executive Vice Chairman from 2021; Trian and the Peltzes hold a roughly 15% stake.
interesting_fact: He previously served on the board of ARG Holding Corporation, the former parent of Arby's, from 2012 to 2015, one of several restaurant brands in the Peltz family's orbit.
deep_cut_fact: Outside finance he is a trustee of the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York.
notes: MarketScreener lists his Wendy's director/vice-chair role as ending in 2025 while Wendy's bio page still shows him; check the latest proxy. Media route is via Trian or Wendy's corporate communications.

name: Edward Smolyansky
current_role: Founder, Pure Culture Naturals (kefir brand); largest individual shareholder of Lifeway Foods (LWAY)
profile: Son of Lifeway Foods founders Michael and Ludmila Smolyansky, Edward worked at the family kefir company for two decades as controller, CFO, COO and director until 2022. He remains Lifeway's largest shareholder (~16%) and has led a public campaign for board change, and in 2025 launched his own kefir brand, Pure Culture.
interesting_fact: After leaving Lifeway he started a direct kefir competitor, Pure Culture, unveiled at Natural Products Expo West 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His family brought kefir to the American mainstream after emigrating from the Soviet Union; Lifeway was founded in Morton Grove, Illinois in 1986, and Edward grew up speaking Russian at home.
notes: Ongoing, contentious shareholder dispute with Lifeway's board (CEO is his sister Julie Smolyansky); avoid that topic in outreach. Best route is likely via Pure Culture or the press contacts on his shareholder-campaign press releases (e.g. https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2361215/).

name: Tara Lal
profile: Listed by Hurun India (2018) with wealth from Eicher Motors, the Royal Enfield parent controlled by the Vikram Lal family. Authoritative Eicher sources do not name a Tara Lal; one data aggregator links a 'Tara Lal Vikram' to Eicher's promoter holding company, so she is likely a passive Lal-family shareholder.
notes: Could not confirm identity or role from reliable sources. Not a public figure; the operating family leader is Siddhartha Lal (Executive Chairman, Eicher Motors) https://eicher.in/about-us/siddhartha-lal

name: Percy Sorabji Chowdhry
current_role: Executive Director and promoter, Keystone Realtors Ltd (Rustomjee Group), Mumbai
profile: One of the three promoters of Mumbai developer Keystone Realtors, which builds under the Rustomjee brand, alongside chairman-MD Boman Irani and Chandresh Mehta. He has been on Keystone's board since January 1999, making him its longest-serving director; the company listed on Indian exchanges in 2022.
interesting_fact: He is the longest-serving director on Keystone Realtors' board, appointed 3 January 1999.
notes: Very low public profile; Boman Irani is the group's public face. Approach via Rustomjee corporate communications/investor relations.

name: Raffaele Zagari
current_role: CEO and Chairman, Augustea Group (Naples); Director, Star Bulk Carriers (NASDAQ: SBLK)
profile: Neapolitan shipowner from the Cafiero-Zagari family behind Augustea Group, which he has led since 2010 after running its chartering desk from 1997. In 2018 Augustea sold 16 dry-bulk ships to Star Bulk largely for shares, which brought him onto Star Bulk's board and created his SBLK stake.
interesting_fact: The 2018 sale of 16 Augustea bulkers to Star Bulk was paid mostly in Star Bulk stock, turning the Zagari family into major shareholders of one of the largest US-listed dry-bulk owners.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he cut his teeth at Zodiac Maritime Agencies in London (1996-97) and earlier at Blenheim Shipping, where he gained hands-on experience at Japanese shipyards; he holds a diploma in commercial shipping operations from London Guildhall University.
notes: Dates for his Augustea CEO role vary by source (2010 per Star Bulk, 2015 per a third-party case study). Route via Augustea Group or Star Bulk IR.

name: Clinton Bybee
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director (listed by some sources as Emeritus), ARCH Venture Partners
profile: Clint Bybee co-founded ARCH Venture Partners, the early-stage firm spun out of the University of Chicago/Argonne tech-transfer effort, and has invested in advanced materials, semiconductors, photonics and infrastructure tech. His SEC-reported 10% stakes in Neumora, Lyell and Boundless Bio reflect ARCH funds' biotech holdings rather than personal operating roles.
interesting_fact: He is an organizing member and the first President of the Texas Venture Capital Association, and has served on boards including RFID chipmaker Impinj.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he worked as a production engineer at Amoco, and he managed a venture fund for the State of Illinois before co-founding ARCH; he holds a Texas A&M engineering degree and a University of Chicago MBA.
notes: Relevant to energy/infrastructure-tech angle (advanced materials, photonics, semiconductors). Ownership filings are as ARCH fund manager. Based in Austin per Crunchbase.

name: Andrew C Dodson
current_role: Managing Partner, Parthenon Capital; Director, loanDepot, Inc. (NYSE: LDI)
profile: Andrew Dodson is a managing partner and investment-committee member at growth-equity firm Parthenon Capital, which he joined in 2005 and where he heads the San Francisco office. He represents Parthenon, an early backer of loanDepot, on the lender's board.
interesting_fact: He has served on the board of loanDepot's operating company, loanDepot.com LLC, since December 2009, when the mortgage lender was a young startup, well before its 2021 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Before Parthenon he was a consultant at Bain & Company (2004-2005); he is a Duke graduate with a Harvard MBA.
notes: Private-equity investor with low public profile; route via Parthenon Capital.

name: Samuel M Mencoff
current_role: Founding Partner and Senior Advisor, Madison Dearborn Partners; Lead Independent Director, Packaging Corporation of America; Chair, Brown University Health
profile: Sam Mencoff spent 11 years at First Chicago Venture Capital before co-founding Chicago private-equity firm Madison Dearborn Partners in 1992, later serving as co-CEO; MDP's 1999 buyout of Packaging Corporation of America put him on PCA's board, where he is lead independent director. He also founded industrial holding company Temple Hall Group.
interesting_fact: He served as Brown University's 21st chancellor (2016-2024) and in 2025 became board chair of Brown University Health, Rhode Island's largest integrated academic medical system.
deep_cut_fact: He studied anthropology at Brown (BA 1978), is a commissioner of the Smithsonian's National Portrait Gallery, and chairs the Art Institute of Chicago's Committee on American Art.
notes: Past boards include Great Lakes Dredge & Dock, Huntway Refining, Smurfit Kappa and Boise Cascade (industrial/energy-adjacent). Route via Madison Dearborn Partners.

name: Michael R. Ivas
current_role: Senior Vice President, Corporate Controller (and Principal Accounting Officer), Amphenol Corporation
profile: A CPA who joined connector and sensor maker Amphenol in 2001 and has been its Corporate Controller since 2015, designated principal accounting officer in 2025. His stake has grown with Amphenol's surge as a key supplier of high-speed interconnect and power products for AI data centers.
interesting_fact: Amphenol, where he oversees accounting, has become one of the major beneficiaries of the AI data-center buildout through its high-speed cable, connector and power-distribution products.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Amphenol in 2001 as Director of Internal Audit after seven years at PricewaterhouseCoopers (senior audit manager); he holds a BBA in accounting from Westfield State University.
notes: Finance executive, not a public-facing figure; outreach via Amphenol investor relations/corporate communications.

name: Jason Chung
current_role: Chief Financial Officer (since March 1, 2026; formerly EVP, Head of Corporate Development & Strategy), Riot Platforms
profile: Former Nomura M&A managing director who joined bitcoin miner Riot Platforms in June 2022 to run corporate development, capital markets and IR, becoming EVP in 2023. Promoted to CFO effective March 2026 as Riot pushes to convert its large Texas power footprint into AI/HPC data-center capacity.
interesting_fact: His CFO promotion was framed around Riot's pivot to AI/high-performance computing, leveraging its large power-secured Texas sites (e.g. Corsicana) for data-center use.
deep_cut_fact: Before Riot he was a Managing Director in M&A at Nomura (2017-2022); he is a CFA charterholder with a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Toronto.
notes: Highly relevant to energy/data-center podcast (bitcoin mining to AI/HPC conversion). Has spoken at Consensus Hong Kong. Media contact listed: Becca Rincon; IR: Joshua Kane.

name: Pravin Dugel
current_role: Executive Chairman, President and CEO, Ocular Therapeutix (NASDAQ: OCUL)
profile: Retina surgeon who built Retinal Consultants of Arizona into a major clinical-trial practice and was President of IVERIC Bio before joining Ocular Therapeutix as executive chairman in February 2024, adding CEO in April 2024. He is steering the company's bet on Axpaxli, a sustained-release implant for wet AMD and diabetic retinopathy.
interesting_fact: He calls himself 'a very proud refugee and immigrant': his family left Nepal when he was four; he went to boarding school in England, finished high school in New York and became a US citizen in medical school.
deep_cut_fact: He trained under retina legend J. Donald M. Gass, whom he called 'the finest physician I have ever known'; and when he joined Retinal Consultants of Arizona in 1994 it had just three physicians and 12 employees. He is also a wine-tasting enthusiast.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (OIS). Elected to Orbis International board (https://www.pr.com/press-release/731183). Route via Ocular Therapeutix IR/communications.

name: Masi Niccolo De
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, IonQ (NYSE: IONQ); Director, Rush Street Interactive
profile: Niccolo de Masi is a Cambridge-trained physicist turned serial tech CEO (Glu Mobile, Monstermob, Resideo) and SPAC sponsor whose dMY Technology Group III took quantum-computing company IonQ public in 2021 (also Rush Street Interactive, Genius Sports, Planet). He joined IonQ's board in 2021, became CEO in February 2025 and chairman in August 2025, driving an acquisition-led expansion.
interesting_fact: Through the dMY SPAC series he took several companies public, including IonQ, Rush Street Interactive, Genius Sports and Planet, and says he has raised more than $3 billion in equity for companies he has led.
deep_cut_fact: He studied physics at Cambridge (BA and MSc), and one of his first jobs was at Siemens Solar, before Technicolor and his move into mobile gaming.
notes: High-profile, media-friendly CEO; good fit for tech/data-center angle (quantum + space division). Note the IR page lists investors@ionq.com while the release says investors@ionq.co.

name: Vincent Drouillard
current_role: General Counsel, AerCap Holdings N.V. (NYSE: AER), Dublin
profile: Aviation-finance lawyer who has been General Counsel of AerCap, the world's largest aircraft lessor, since June 2018. He joined ILFC in 2004 (rising to Head of Legal EMEA), stayed through AerCap's 2014 acquisition of ILFC, and headed legal for leasing 2015-2018; his wealth comes from AerCap equity awards.
interesting_fact: He has spent more than two decades in aircraft leasing, moving from ILFC into AerCap when it bought ILFC in 2014, the deal that created the industry's largest lessor.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, holds law degrees from King's College London, Paris I Pantheon-Sorbonne and Paris X Nanterre, and is admitted to both the New York and California bars.

public_contacts.value: AerCap Media Center (press contacts listed on press releases)

notes: In-house lawyer, not public-facing; outreach via AerCap corporate communications.

name: Robert S Wetherbee
current_role: Director, GATX Corporation; former CEO (2019-2024) and Executive Chairman (2024-May 2026) of ATI Inc.
profile: Bob Wetherbee led specialty-materials maker ATI as CEO from 2019 to July 2024, reshaping it from a cyclical metals producer into an aerospace-and-defense materials supplier, then served as Executive Chairman until retiring from ATI's board at the May 14, 2026 annual meeting. He continues as a director of railcar lessor GATX.
interesting_fact: ATI credits him with transforming the company into an 'aerospace and defense powerhouse'; on handing over, he praised successor Kimberly Fields, who became board chair in 2026.
notes: Retired from ATI in May 2026, so ATI IR is only an indirect route; GATX investor relations (https://ir.gatx.com) is an alternative. Search budget ran out before a sourced deep-cut fact was found.

name: Charles William Griege Jr.
current_role: Founding Partner and CIO, Roaring Blue Lion Capital Management; Director, GBank Financial Holdings (GBFH), Las Vegas
profile: Dallas-area bank-stock investor who founded Roaring Blue Lion Capital Management in 2005 and launched its Bank Consolidation Fund in 2011 to play post-crisis bank M&A. Earlier he was a partner at Atlas Capital (grew it from ~$50M to ~$650M) and an MD at SoundView Technology Group; he has sat on GBank's board since October 2021.
interesting_fact: He has been investing in bank stocks since 1986 and co-founded a CLO Opportunity Fund in 2009, at the depths of the financial crisis.
deep_cut_fact: Before business school he spent three years at the Federal Home Loan Bank of Dallas, working with savings banks in the hardest-hit US region and watching the creation of the Resolution Trust Corporation; he holds a Vanderbilt economics BA and a Columbia MBA with honors.

public_contacts.value: hsledgesarnor@g.bank (GBank General Counsel & Corporate Secretary, listed as Investor Relations contact)

notes: Niche fund manager with low media profile; route via Roaring Blue Lion or GBank IR.

name: Robyn Tannenbaum
current_role: President and CIO, Advanced Flower Capital (AFCG, formerly AFC Gamma); President, Sunrise Realty Trust (SUNS)
profile: Lender-executive who co-leads the Tannenbaum-founded platform of Advanced Flower Capital (cannabis-industry lender) and Sunrise Realty Trust (Southern US commercial real-estate lender), serving as AFC President since 2023, CIO since 2024 and SRT President since 2024. Earlier she was head of investor relations at Fifth Street and a healthcare M&A VP at CIT Group.
interesting_fact: Between Fifth Street and AFC she founded REC Investor Relations, a boutique IR and marketing consultancy for healthcare and financial-services companies (2017-2020).
deep_cut_fact: She graduated summa cum laude from Lehigh University with a B.S. in Finance, a marketing concentration and a public-relations minor.
notes: Married to company founder Leonard Tannenbaum (AFC/SRT chairman); she previously ran investor relations, so is comfortable with media. Route via AFC or Sunrise Realty Trust IR (no published email captured; web search budget exhausted).

name: Paresh Patel
current_role: Chairman and CEO, HCI Group (NYSE: HCI); Chairman and CEO, Exzeo Group (NYSE: XZO)
profile: Cambridge-trained engineer who co-founded Tampa-based Florida homeowners insurer HCI Group (Homeowners Choice, TypTap), serving as chairman since 2007 and CEO since 2011. He also leads HCI's insurance-software arm Exzeo Group, which went public on the NYSE in November 2025.
interesting_fact: He spun HCI's in-house insurance technology into a separate public company, Exzeo Group, which IPO'd on the NYSE in November 2025 with him as chairman and CEO.
deep_cut_fact: He personally developed HCI's original insurance policy administration systems; he holds bachelor's and master's degrees in electronic engineering from the University of Cambridge, and was a founder of NorthStar Bank in Tampa.
notes: Tech-founder angle (insurtech) rather than energy. Route via HCI Group investor relations.

name: Ning Jun
profile: Listed on the 2008 Hurun China list with wealth from Hwagain Group (pulp/paper and sugar), the Guangxi-based paper maker with mills in Nanning, Guangxi and Ganzhou, Jiangxi that has received IFC financing. Could not confirm Ning Jun's current role at the group from reliable sources.
notes: Only one listing (Hurun 2008); company background per IFC disclosure https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/30021/guangxi-hwagain-group-co-ltd . Hwagain website unreachable and web search budget exhausted; Chinese-language sources needed.
